FOREWORD the draft finalized This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after by the Livestock Feeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. proteins has been suggested for many years as a means to alleviate protein Algae have also been used in animal feeds generally and in specialised aqua-feeds in ), particular as a non-conventional protein source. Spirulina, a blue green alga ( cyanobacterium B-complex vitamins, particularly is characterised by high content of protein, p-carotene, shows it cyanocobalamine and gamma-linolenic acid. The amino acid pattern of this protein to be of reasonably good quality and it may be added to enrich various feed formulations. The percentage of essential amino acids in Spirulina platensis is reported as lysine 4.8 percent, histimethionine 2.5 percent, leucine dine 1.8 percent, arginine 6.5 percent, threonine 6.2 percent, 7-1 percent, isoleucine 6.7 percent and phenylalanine 4.9 percent. In view of high nutrient content besides proteins, Spirulina is marketed internationally in natural and health foods, in This alga has also been approved by FDA of specialised animal feeds and also in cosmetics. the United States for being used a natural food. Spirulina of species platensis maxima and fusiformis are commonly used for the commercial production of feed grade alga. This standard is therefore, being formulated to ensure production of Spiruha of certain minimum quality.
shortage.

Use of algal

Peed grade alga Spirulina is produced with suitable nutrient medium with chemicals or in diluted and treated effluents from biogas plants or domestic sewage. Though there are variations in the details of the manufacturing processes, the production of feed grade alga basically involves the following steps: a) b) c) d) e) Selection of suitable strains of alga; Preparation of nutrient medium and specified culture conditions; Cultivation of selected alga in open culture ponds under defined conditions; Separation of grown alga by filtration and washing to get rid of residual nutrients; Suitable drying to flakes or fine powder.

and

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules fur rounding off numerical values ( revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Description The material shall be in the form of dried powder, granules or flakes. It shall be of uniform dark blue-green colour and shall have the characteristic taste and odour ( mild resembling dried greens ) of good quality alga, free from any unpleasant musty or putrid smell. It shall be dry and free from lumps and from extraneous matter, added colour and deleterious substances. It shall also be free from rodent contamination, visible mould growth, insect infestation and toxic materials and heavy metals like lead, copper, mercury and arsenic. Pesticide residues shall be within permissible limits. NOTE -The appearance, taste and odour of alga

B

( Clause 4.4 )
BIOASSAY B-l PROCEDURE B-l.1 Test Organism Used PROCEDURE TO TEST TOXIC FORMS OF ALGAE

Na, PO, NaCl ( Crude sea salt ) MgSO, 7H,O FeSO,
B-l.4 Testing Spirulina Cultures

25 mg/l 25 mg/l 10 mg/l 2 mgll

Scenedesmus B-l.2

acutus (green algae ) Test Culture

Method of Raising

Genetically pure strain of Scenedesmus acutus maintained as stock culture on agar slants with the medium as given in B-l.3 and periodically subcultured ( every 30 days ). Liquid cultmes of Scendesmus is raised from the stock in 250 ml Erlenmeyer flasks in the same medium ( each flask to contain 200 ml ). The flasks are placed in rotary shaker ( 30-40 rpm ), at temperature ( 25 28�C ) with illumination provided by tubelights 4-5 K lux. The growth rate is monitored as optical density at 560 hrn and the algal biomass expressed as mg dry algae/100 ml culture read from standard growth curve ( 0.1 OD=lOO mg dry algae ). B-l.3 Nutrient Medium medium is used for grow-

Cultures are drawn from the culture basins and filtered in 60-80 micron Nylon mesh to remove the Spirulina cells and the filtrate is centrifuged at 1 000 rpm for 10 minutes to concentrate other algal forms present in the filtrate. Ten ml of the sedimented filtrate is used in the test for toxicity by adding to the Erlenmeyer flask containing growing Scenedesmus cultures at 0.1 OD. Six replicates of control ( Scenedesmus alone ) and experimental ( Scenedesmus + 10 ml sedimented filtrate ) were grown in flasks ( B-l.2 ) and growth rate compared for a period of 5 days. Measurements of growth are recorded at OD every day. Reduction of growth of Scenedesmus culture by more than 10 percent as compared to control indicates inhibition of algal growth which is attributable to toxic algae being present in cultures.

SAMPLING OF FEED GRADE ALGA D-l GENERAL REQUIREMENI'S OF SAMPLING D-l.0 In drawing, preparing, storing and handling samples, the following precautions and directions shall be observed. D-l.1 Samples shall be taken in a protected place not exposed to damp air, dust or soot. D-l.2 The sampling and dry when used. instrument shall be clean ( or his representative his representative ). ) and the supplier ( or

D-2 SCALE OF SAMPLlNG D-2.1 Lot All the containers in a consignment belonging to the same batch manufacture shall constitute a lot. D-2.2 The number containers to be tested from the lot shall depend on the oize of the lot and shall be in accordance with Table 3. Table 3
Numb; &I%nGners

D-l.3 Precautions shall be taken to protect the samples, the material being sampled, the sampling instrument and the containers being sampled from adventitious contamination. D-l.4 Samples shall be placed in clean, free from odour and dry glass containers. The containers shall be of such a size that they are almost completely filled by the sample. D-l.5 Each container shall be sealed air-tight after filling and marked with full details of sampling, batch or code number, name of the manufacturer and other important particulars of the consignment. D-l.6 Samples shaI1 be stored in such a manner that the temperature of the material does not vary unduly from the normal temperature. D-l.7 Sampling shall be done by a person agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier and in the presence of the purchaser

The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and Standard marked products are also continuously checked by operated by the producer. Details of conditions under BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
